column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check

Article says Dürer died 6 April 1528 in lead; death not told in given text beyond dates. Article says 'Within three months of his marriage' - marriage year not given in given part (1494 per heading), not stated. Printmaker point: article says Raphael, Titian and Parmigianino collaborated with printmakers, inspired by his success.

Entry says Cicero's defence of Sextus Roscius was in 80 BCE; the article gives no year, so none is printed. | Article gives 1135 BC (Cato) and 1136 BC (Pliny the Younger tradition); both attributed. | Left out: church and palace catalogue, notable people, twin towns, 2021 population, Greek name forms.
Omitted StB informant claim, tributes list, long thought section details. Article says Cabral shot dead in Conakry; desc consistent.

Entry says 322 BCE defeat of Athenian fleet by Macedonians; article only says Athens and Macedonia fought the naval Battle of Amorgos, so the text does not give the winner. Entry says Minoa traditionally settled from Samos; article says a Samian colony led by Semonides, not tied to a city. Left out 2021 population.

Article dates the activity c. 760-755 BC 'according to the Bible'; entry says 8th century BCE, compatible. Article notes Gary Rendsburg's view that the Teqoaʿ was in Galilee, while the entry says Tekoa in Judah; left out so the page does not disagree. Left out: modern political allusions, Islamic tradition.
Article lead gives birth c. 585, body c. 573; entry says c. 573. Birth and age omitted. Article dates start of Egypt campaign 12 December 639; entry says 640s: only 640 and 641 events printed.

Article: 'his death was ruled a murder by medical examiners; three royal aides executed after irregular trials'. Text uses neutral inquiry/trial facts. Left out: allegations about Bhumibol, Pridi, and Tsuji Masanobu (Stevenson) as unproven. Desc says 'found shot dead six months after returning in December 1945': consistent.

Skipped for lack of historical substance. | SKIP: article is almost wholly current civic administration, transport and sport; its history is three dated facts (1799 headquarters, municipality 1869, corporation 2004) and it does not mention the entry's reservoir, Vijayanagara, Nolamba or poligar history

The article excerpt does not mention suppression by the Bolsheviks or communists in Spain (entry's claims) nor Kropotkin's role in detail, so those are neither repeated nor contradicted. Entry's date 'c. 1840': the article gives Proudhon's What Is Property? of 1840.

Article: age at death 90.5 (Malalas) vs 88 (Victor); desc says c. 430 birth; text gives only Victor's 88 attributed - but 88 implies c.430, consistent. Desc mentions Ghassanids/treaty c. 502: not in article, omitted. Desc says 'Miaphysite', article 'Monophysite': text follows article.

Article says 'Around 1 BC ... founded by the Jinhan people'; written as 1 BCE. Entry's King Gongmin refuge in 1361 is not in the article and not repeated. Left out: population figures, universities, sister cities, people list (some living), the 1999 visit.

Article says imprisoned, then released 'Christmas Day 1967' and calls the junta 'seven-year'; entry is silent on these. | Entry: PM 1981-1989 and 1993-1996, PASOK founded 1974; matches article. | Left out: personal life, terrorism section, details of the 1985 stabilisation, and the lead's sharper judgements (corruption 'black sheep' etc.), kept to attributed 'critics'.

Article: Galicia expulsion 'August 1189 or 1190'; kept as given. Entry date c. 1177 matches article's 'around 1177'. | Left out: Hum, Teutonic Knights, Latin Empire hopes, Austrian treaties, Mstislav Mstislavich episodes, the 1233 promise.
Article: 'his reign ... 1282 to 1328', consistent with desc. Desc says Theodore inherited Montferrat in 1306; article gives no year, so not repeated. Desc 'hired' Catalan Company consistent.

Entry says Chios recovered 1329 and Pelekanos 1329; article: Pelekanon 10 or 15 June 1329 (hedged by 'June 1329'). Entry 'annexed Thessaly and Epirus' consistent. | Left out: marriages and children, Syrgiannes episode, Trebizond daughter, Ibn Battuta, civil war dates.

Entry says the castles passed to Ferdinand III in the 1220s through the Almohad prince al-Bayyasi; article says the Muslim king of Baeza handed them over in 1225 and that some scholars date it differently; written with that hedge and without naming al-Bayyasi. Population 35,619 (2024) rounded.
Entry says built 'late twelfth century'; article agrees. Article gives no date for the Ayutthaya sack; none printed. | Left out: popular culture list, Ta Prohm roundels, Prasat Chrung, distances.

Article says last Peterborough copying to 1131, and 'one case' actively updated in 1154 (entry: Peterborough reaches 1154); both stated without linking the 1154 entry to Peterborough explicitly in the article. Article says manuscript G (A2) was destroyed in the fire at 'Ashburnham House in London' / 'Westminster'; the location left out. Seventh manuscript described as burned (G).

Article says Ani was abandoned by the 17th century; the entry says by the 18th, so the abandonment date is left out. Article's timeline gives Zakarian Armenia from 1201 and Georgia from 1199/1201; entry says Shaddadids and Zakarids ruled after Byzantine and Seljuk conquests, consistent. Entry says Ashot III made it capital in 961; article gives no founder for 961.
Entry says she acted with Philip in government during his minority; article says regent in lead but Baldwin guardian: I avoided 'regent'. Left out 2017 and 2024 political items.
Entry says Annaberg 'founded in 1496' and 'one of the largest towns in Saxony' (article: Germany, 8,000); entry says Ries lived there, article only monument and museum: none of these printed.
Desc mentions the Edict of Union of 1532: not in the article, omitted. Article says Claude married Francis 'in the year following Anne's death'; text avoids the year.
Desc consistent with article. The article's intro 'accompanied Gournay 1743' is a slip, ignored.

Article has Smetona 'authoritarian head of state from 1926'; desc 'returned to power after the coup of December 1926' consistent. Desc says he fled abroad after the ultimatum, died in US 1944: consistent. 'Memel surrendered 1939' stated in article ('The following year' after 1938). Jewish policy sentence hedged as article's account.

Article says Pavelić 'schemed' and the Ustaše founded 'in 1929'; entry fine. Article is inconsistent on the first attempt on Alexander (1933 failed, 1934 Marseille); written without the 1933 attempt. Left out: honours, post-war Vatican allegations, final-days details.

Article says Antigonus's brief rule 'emerged as most powerful'; entry says he sought to reunite the empire; both consistent. Article says Perinthus anecdote is about 'an Antigonus', hedged in text. Article text on the Third War: Gaza and Babylonian War 311-309 compressed.
Entry says reigned 175-164, article same. 2 Maccabees' figure of eighty thousand killed left out.
Desc says 'defeated near Oryol'; article says Orel and Voronezh. Article gives birth as 16 December New Style / 4 December Old Style; text gives 4 December as the article's early-life section does.

Desc says cited as part of cultural flowering of Vienna: not in article, omitted. Article's lead says 'accidentally killed by a soldier after WWII' and gives 15 Sept 1945 death date; consistent with desc dates 1883-1945. Section 1 says Schoenberg taught from Bach etc: article says Webern was inspired by Schoenberg's emphasis on structure in teaching composition.

Entry says 'about twenty years' on the northern frontier then withdrew; article says abandoned only eight years after completion, withdrawal 162 (text gives 162 and 'within two decades'). Article gives 16 forts in one place and nineteen in another: no count given. Entry says land of the Damnonii: not in article, left out. Entry dated 142, same as article.

Article gives birth August 1489, also says date uncertain; desc c. 1489; wrote 'around 1489'. Article dates Cathedral Assumption variously (three years after 1520-21 dome; selected works 1526-1530); wrote 'about three years later' following the article text; may be omitted if flagged.

Article says Tarqui 27 Feb 1829 and presidency 1825-1828; consistent with desc. Desc says 'resigned in 1828': consistent. Plot attribution in article: Obando named by confessions; text hedged with 'attributed' and the lead's 'speculation'.

Article says the name Diego Suarez came from Diogo (Dias) and Soares, and that Antomabokala, former capital of Ankarana, acquired it; the Antomabokala point is left out as unclear. Treaty of 1885 and base from 1942 consistent with the entry.
Article says Yin ruins were discovered in 1899 and excavated in following decades; entry says excavations since 1928. Left out both. 'Seven dynasties' capital' and tourism lists left out.

Entry says suspension 1986 and 'mid-1980s' ban; article: dispute 1984, Buchanan February 1985, suspension announced 1986. Consistent. | Left out per present-day rule: events after 2010, AUKUS, Taiwan section, Iraq and Afghanistan contributions.
Article says 'Apelles of Kos', 'probably born at Colophon'; desc states Colophon flatly - birthplace deliberately left out.

Entry dates c. 15 - c. 100 CE; article gives Philostratus c. 3 BCE - c. 97 CE and Dzielska c. 40 CE birth (from Cassius Dio). No dates printed in text. Entry mentions Taxila under a Parthian king: not in the article extract, left out.

Desc says 'Popes have lived there since their return from Avignon'; the article says the popes after 1377 first lived at Santa Maria in Trastevere and Santa Maria Maggiore and that the apartments have been the official residence since the 17th century. Text gives the article's 17th-century statement only; editor to decide whether the desc needs fixing. Left out recent details (closures to tourists, Pope Francis and Leo XIV residence, 2021 gallery) as present-day matter.

Article dates the confederation 1378–1508; entry says second half of the fifteenth century. The 1378 start left out. Article's Safavid dates: Ismail defeated them 1501 (Nakhchivan) and conquered Diyarbakir 1507-8; entry says 'early sixteenth century' - consistent. Fine: article has two contradictory Rustam reign dates; omitted.

The article is general hydrogeology and says nothing of the Garamantes, foggaras or Safavid qanats named in the entry; none of that is repeated or contradicted. Left out: classification detail (storativity), depletion statistics, offshore finds after 2013.
Entry says Byzantines recovered Cilicia and Antioch (969); article extract does not mention them, so text does not either.

Article contradicts itself on capital (Petra initially, then Bosra); entry says Bostra; text avoids naming a capital. Article gives the Palaestina division as second half of 4th century (exact time debated).

Entry says Island Carib is the ancestor of Garifuna; the article describes Garifuna as arising from forced migration of mixed Arawak, Carib and African people and groups Island Carib with Garifuna in one classification. Text does not state the relationship. | Left out: speaker counts, classification tables, phonology, Proto-Arawakan, the Cusabo/Congaree possibility.
Entry dates c. 428-c. 347 BCE; article gives 435/410 and 360/350 BC: no dates printed.

Article calls the taifa family Banu Jizrun (Jizrunis); entry says Banu Khizrun. Text says only 'a Berber family of the Zenata'. Entry says annexed by the Abbadids; article says by al-Mutadid of Seville in 1053 (same dynasty). Left out sights lists, festivals, cuisine.

Article uses BC; converted to BCE. Ephialtes: article hedges ('may have'), desc states flatly; kept article's hedge with 462/461 vs desc 462 — close; check. Article gives Paul 'Acts 17:16-34'. Hill also mentioned as 'Hill of Ares'.
Entry says 'regarded as the oldest town in Thuringia'; article says 'one of the oldest': I used the article wording. Omitted WWII POW camp details.

Desc says Arnulf defeated Vikings 'on the Dyle in 891'; article says he repelled them in September 891 and built a castle on an island in the Dijle after; text avoids place. Desc says Magyar raids devastated after death: not in article; omitted. Article says Arnulf's stroke 896; also rumours of poisoning omitted.

Entry: c. 845-c. 907; article: Gesta says 907, Kristó says 900 or later; the latter is not printed, 907 is attributed to the Gesta. | Entry says Árpád led the Hungarians 'after his father Álmos' across the Carpathians around 895; article says crossing in 895/896 under pressure from Pechenegs and that Álmos's fate is disputed. Left out those disputes. | Left out: Curta's theory, Ja'far Tarikh, the Gesta quotation, burial place.

Article given only as lead and openings. Moroccan arquebusiers at Tondibi 1591, Adal Sultanate and Portuguese in Africa (in desc) are not in the file, so not repeated. Article says matchlock dating is disputed; I recorded both views.

Desc: Panagia Parigoritissa 13th century; article: built c. 1290 (consistent). Article spells 'Parigoritissa' and 'Paregoretissa'. Folk-song fame of the bridge not in article, omitted. Baden-style thin material not an issue.

Desc says he reconquered Egypt in 343 BCE; the article says probably 340 or 339 BCE (and elsewhere implies he was in Babylon by 341). Text gives no year for the reconquest. Desc says reigned from 358 BCE; article 359/58: text gives no accession year. Article's sentence 'Egypt back after six decades' kept. Inconsistent article: 330,000-man army and 40,000 dead at Sidon given as stated; the first omitted.

Article dates composition between the 1st and 3rd century CE (Olivelle/McClish) and rejects the Chanakya identification; the entry says 'traditionally attributed', and the text says only that scholarship questions the identification. Entry says 'debated'. No contradiction left in text.

Article on the Balkans is garbled (spy plan, Bobovo); only the expulsion from Pljevlja during the Herzegovina uprising is used. Concrete reconstruction and 'devised chronology' (in the entry) are not in the article, not repeated. Article gives no date of Margaret's death and no death narrative, so no 'Death and legacy' section. Article: 'Evans was first to define Linear A and B' and says Evans dated Linear B tablets to before the 15th century collapse (left out). Birth place and date from the article.

Article does not say the town passed to Brandenburg-Prussia, only Principality of Halberstadt and Prussian Province of Saxony; entry's text not contradicted. Olearius born place: article lists him as notable person of Aschersleben, birth town not stated explicitly - check.

Earthquake death toll in the entry is not in the given part of the article; not printed. Article gives population 1,030,063 (2022 census); I wrote about one million. Nyýazow-era renaming and 'White City' attribution omitted.

Entry: d. c. 700 and 'ruled until about 700'. Article gives Moskov 668-695 and others 700 or 701, and the Nominalia's 61 years; none printed, the text says only that chronologies differ. | Left out: Hunnish/Oghur language paragraph (about languages, not Asparuh), Antarctic Asparuh Peak, Djagfar Tarikhy.
Article says founding in 1466 but full separation only in 1502; entry says c. 1466-1556; text avoids a single founding date. Founder either Mahmud or Qasim I per article.

Entry: r. 585-550 BCE; article gives 553 revolt plus three years of fighting (consistent with 550). Entry says 'according to tradition grandfather of Cyrus'; text reports that modern scholarship rejects this, per article. | Left out: Bel and the Dragon / Darius the Mede identification, dog-suckling explanation, Xenophon.

Entry says forms persisted until Philip II conquered Athens in 338 BCE; the article says Philip led a coalition in 336 BC and that democracy was restored in 307 BC after the Macedonian governors. Those dates are left out so as not to contradict the entry. | Entry already states the 30 percent figure, Solon, Cleisthenes' tribes, Ephialtes and the oligarchic revolutions; not repeated.

Article gives 12.75 million loaded (lead) and, citing Anderson, 12.5 million with 10.7 million surviving; only the lead figures used. Entry says 16th-19th centuries; article dates the coastal trade to the 15th century (1441/1444), mentioned as origin only.
Entry says 'about 102 metres', matches. Left out visitor numbers and present rankings.

Last paragraph of article concerns a July 2026 political event: excluded by the present-day rule. | SKIP: article is short; its background repeats the entry and the rest (tune-only use after 1973, end in 1990, Kohl's rejection, a 1995 mistaken playing) is under about 250 words of substance, and the lyrics section is empty
Article gives exile in Mexico 1929-30 and EMECU spiritism; omitted.

Article gives Augustus's Polish reign as 1697-1706 and 1709-1733; text avoids the exact years and says he gave up the throne in 1706 (Altranstädt) and returned after Poltava 1709, consistent with desc. Desc 'ruling for most of 1697-1733' kept untouched. | Article calls the 360-380 children claim variously 365 or 382 in a later section; text uses the lead's 360-380.

Article says election 'by a small minority on 5 October 1733'; vote counts 12,000 vs 3,000 given in article. Article calls Augustus the lover... nothing contradictory with desc. Desc says election owed to Russian and Austrian intervention, consistent.

Desc: 'set to its present tune 1799'; article: first documented use 1799. Used 'first documented use'. Omitted films, recent live performances (2020, 2022) and current-affairs uses. Burns/Watson 'James Watson' appears both as ballad printer (1711) and in a list of poets (the article's own list).
Desc consistent (consul 379). Article says Gratian 'bestowed the consulship'. Cento nuptialis described neutrally. Article's Paulinus of Pella grandson omitted.
Entry says annexed one by one 1880-1901; article gives final annexation 1900, so the final year is left unstated. Population left out (article gives 6,965 and 6,820 for 2012).

Entry says 'formed in the 1890s'; article says founded 1891. Text does not state a founding year for the party itself, only the colonial labour parties from 1891 and 1893. | Left out: current government, current leaders, donors, youth wing, election results, Country Labor, policy caucuses, factions.

Left out as recent or current: leaders and results since 2017, the Ibiza affair, 2024 election. Entry's founding in April 1945, the chancellors from Figl to Kurz and the federation of leagues are not in the article and not repeated.

Entry says outside pomerium until the reign of Claudius and cult of Vertumnus 'after 264 BCE'; article says Vortumnus c. 264, so no year is printed for it. Claudius is not in the article, so not mentioned. | Left out: Cacus myth, literary cameos, Skutsch theory, the wall's date puzzle.
Article gives no birth year; entry c. 390 not printed. Article is inconsistent on deposition (Senate 17 Sept vs Piacenza battle in October); kept to the Piacenza date.

The article says nothing of Amda Seyon or the river as a frontier of the Ethiopian Empire, which is in the entry; nothing on that was added. Left out pollution, climate and recent population material as current affairs.

Entry says renamed after the battle of 1824; article gives the decree on 15 February 1825 (text uses that, consistent). Article misprints battle as 9 December 1924 (text uses 1824). Left out Wari dates (article gives 500-900 and 600-1000), economy figures, rankings and 2020s sports plans. Etymology 'explained below' is awkward but the renaming is told in History.

Desc says Ayutthaya 'sacked Angkor in the fifteenth century' and 'expanded at the expense of the Khmer Empire'; article says Ayutthaya attacked Angkor in the 1430s but did NOT sack it (installed a short-lived puppet ruler). Left Angkor and Khmer out entirely. Article: 'Fra Mauro map circa 1450' vs '1459' (not used). Desc 'central Thailand' ok.

Article says Soviet intervention was 'with the consent of Amin's government' - left out. Name rendering 'Comrade of the Workers' kept as article gives. Left out Mitrokhin affair claim and other contested details.

Article gives the fall of Jerusalem as 597 BCE and the return under Cyrus as 538 BCE (Ezra); the entry gives 539 BCE, so the end of the exile is told without a year. Article is inconsistent on the Second Temple (c. 537 in lead; 521-516 in the account); left out.

Article says Bacolod was converted from municipality to city in 1938 (Etymology) - omitted. Article states MassKara Festival variously third week vs fourth Sunday of October; wrote 'in October'. Desc 'Republic of Negros' not in the shown article text except 'Cantonal Republic of Negros'; article calls it Cantonal Republic; I did not name the Republic of Negros. Article lead says 'Negros Island Region' - used.

Entry says the princes' residence 'from the 18th century' and a palace built there; article says the counts made it their residence in 1655 and the Baroque palace 1713-1728. The 1655 date is not printed. | Entry names the Arolsen Archives; article calls the institution the International Tracing Service; text uses the article's name only. | Left out: politics, partnerships, events, notable-people list, 2006 document access announcement.

Article gives only the bare Ems Dispatch fact; the detail in desc (Bismarck, William I, French ambassador, July 1870) is not in the article and is not repeated. 'around 9,000 inhabitants' is the article's figure.

Desc says shared between Electoral Palatinate and Baden and seat of army HQ 1917-18: neither is in the article's supplied part; not repeated. Article is truncated; the Michel Mort legend, Faust etc left out. Population omitted deliberately.

Entry says the castle was the grand masters' seat 'from 1527'; article says headquarters from 1526 (lead) and the move of the Deutschmeister in 1525. Dates of the move are left out entirely; Albrecht's resignation is dated only as 'around the time of the move'. | Left out: villages' populations, twinning, notable-people list, sport.

Entry says Pyrmont joined Prussia in 1922; article says the plebiscite and incorporation were on 30 November 1921. Text gives no year for the detachment. Entry mentions Peter the Great and Goethe, not in the article; left out.

Article is thin and partly garbled (1136 'bought the founding of a monastery'); salt-road and archbishop material is in the entry, not the article, so not repeated. Left out: 1999 shooting and 2006 ice rink collapse (recent, not history), notable people list.

Entry gives free imperial city from late 13th century and the 1530 Augsburg Confession; article does not. | SKIP: article has under about 250 words of substance (first record 741, imperial city to 1802, Bavaria 1810, spa town 1961, one 1945 episode, attractions and a list of people); adds little to the entry
SKIP: article under 250 words of substance (358 words in all, mostly repeating the description: Zähringen margraves, 1803, 1806, 1952)

Article says Tilak was the most widely known Indian political leader before Gandhi. Article says Kesari/Mahratta started 1880-81 with Agarkar; text OK. 1897 account: article says he was charged with incitement to murder and also sedition (1897 as 'disaffection of the government'); text says 'for articles in Kesari' per sedition section; Chapekar shooting is noted. Imprisoned Mandalay 1908 to 1914 consistent with desc. 'positions that historians criticise' is the editor to check: article records the positions but not 'historians criticise'; consider rewording. | The time of the 1890 departure from the DES and the 1880 founding of the newspapers: text in first paragraph arranges them out of order but dates are right.

Article: conquered by Ermengol VI of Urgell in 1106; entry says 1105. Article does not mention the 1413 siege. | SKIP: article is about 250 words with little history beyond the entry's own facts; it dates the conquest 1106 where the entry says 1105

Article gives death as March 1185 or before 16 May 1185; text says 1185, no later than 16 May. Mother Agnes's influence left out (sources biased per article). Article says he 'defeated Saladin in 1182' at Le Forbelet; entry mentions Montgisard only.

Article contradicts itself on early ownership: 'in 1162 acquired by the count of Hohenberg' and 'received the title of city from Friedrich der Erlauchte' vs 'established in 1255 by Count Friedrich von Zollern'; 1162 and the title-of-city sentence are left out. Entry says founded as a town by the Zollern in the mid-13th century (consistent with 1255). | Subcamp dated only by the article's 'Second World War (1939-1945)'; text says 1939 to 1945 loosely - check if flagged.
Article says the final agreement involved Serbia 'forced to exchange Macedonia for Albania'; paraphrased cautiously. The article calls Venizelos the spearhead of the league; not repeated.
Entry gives 675 km and two million; consistent.

Desc says Bamenda grew from a German military station in the early 20th century; the article says only colonised by Germany in 1884, so no station date is printed. Omitted the Anglophone crisis (2016 onward), pollution ranking, sports and notable people as current affairs.

Cadusii/Anshan etymology in article is dubious and was left out beyond the bare statement. Article says renamed Pahlavi 1935; desc says Bandar-e Pahlavi 1935-1979 (consistent). Article says Soviet flotilla captured garrison; desc says landed in pursuit of White ships; wrote the article's account without 'pursuit'. Caviar monopoly and tourism rankings omitted.

Article: 'ten in South Africa and ten in South West Africa' in the lead; later 'ten homelands similar to those in South Africa' were established in South West Africa from 1968. Entry's Verwoerd attribution consistent. Left out: comparisons to Palestinian and other present-day cases (current affairs), post-1994 careers of homeland leaders.
Article says he ascended the throne in 1932 (de jure emperor from 1926). Left out marriages, mistresses, honours, coins.

Article says fairs were in mid-February and mid-April; entry says each spring, so months left out. Entry gives fair as 12th-13th centuries; article gives no dates for the fair apart from its end after the 1636 plague - left unstated.
Article does not mention Peter I's conquest of 1100 (in entry); not repeated. Article gives city on Cinca and Vero junction; entry says on the Vero.

Article gives IG Farben's founding as 1921 in a heading and 1925 in the lead; no year printed. Article describes the Auschwitz factory as built by BASF 'leader of the chemical industry of the IG Farben'; written as IG Farben. Killed-prisoner estimate (31,500-33,500) left out because it concerns IG Farben's 23 facilities. Left out: 21st century business, finances, environmental record and lawsuits (current affairs). Entry says BASF 'later developed' ammonia synthesis; article says Haber with Bosch, BASF bought rights - written accordingly.

Desc says drafted by a parliamentary council and that Bavaria's Landtag rejected it; neither is in the file, so omitted. Article says 'adopted 8 May 1949 in Bonn, effect 23 May'; desc 'in force from 23 May 1949' consistent. Article calls the Sonderweg theory 'much contested'; written as 'Some interpreters see'. Amendments 1955 vs article's later 'in 1956' for Bundeswehr (article contradicts itself: 1955 Article 87a and 1956 reintroduction of conscription); only 1955 used, and 'conscription' left out.

Birth: article says late 811 or, for some scholars, the 830s; the entry says 811. Written as 'in 811 by the usual account'. Article says Bari captured by Louis II in 871 with Byzantine help; Photios exiled, Ignatios restored 'one of his first acts'. Article is inconsistent about the dating of Basil's father's name (Bardas/Constantine) - left out. Left out: speculation about same-sex relationships, popular culture.

Article says Suger began about 1135 and the chevet commission was 1140; entry says rebuilding in the 1130s and 1140s, consistent. Article is inconsistent on how many kings are not buried there (three vs five), so no count is given. Left out: present spire reconstruction (recent), burial lists.

Two sections only: the article does not tell her death, so no 'Death and legacy'. Article gives her father as Eliam (Samuel) or Ammiel (Chronicles); both given. Article inconsistent on whether Eliam in 2 Sam 23:34 is the same man - hedged. Left out: rabbinic stories (Satan as a bird, thirteen acts), literature, film, music lists.
Entry credits Assyrians with wheeled armoured rams; article says wheeled frames in the Iron Age generally and shows an Assyrian image. No conflict.
Article's ship numbers conflict: omitted. Entry says Octavian's fleet 'under Agrippa': article says Octavian's fleet led by Agrippa.

Article gives English approx 1,500 men-at-arms and 7,000 archers (Setting) vs Curry 9,000; text attributes. Desc says 'small, exhausted army made up largely of longbowmen'; consistent. Article says Brabant among dead; desc names Duke Anthony of Brabant; text says Brabant only.

Desc says Timur 'won a crushing victory and captured Bayezid, who died in captivity'; article agrees. Article: 'Sivas ... in 1400-01'. 'Bayezid broke off the blockade of Constantinople' as in article.

The article gives inconsistent figures: French army 72,000 (battle section) or 66,000 (casualty section); Allies 85,000 or 89,000. Only the 85,000/72,000 start figures and the casualty counts are printed, no percentages. | The article says Francis II was not on the battlefield although the name 'Three Emperors' refers to three monarchs present; left out. The entry's claim that the battle led to the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire is not in the saved text (it names the Confederation of the Rhine), so not repeated.

The article says the failure forced Hitler to postpone and eventually cancel Sea Lion; the entry says postpone indefinitely. Only the 19 September reduction of work is printed. | German historians count one campaign from July 1940 to May 1941 including the Blitz; British official dating given. Left out: aircraft detail, air-sea rescue, Italian Air Corps, propaganda, attrition disputes, RAF aircrew deaths.
Date: article gives 2 August 216 BC (Macrobius) or 1 July by P. S. Derow; omitted. Carthaginian numbers omitted as unreliable.

Article says the battle ran 13 March to 7 May 1954 and was a two-month siege; casualty figures given inconsistently, so only the prisoner count is used. Left out: Khe Sanh comparison, popular culture, tourism.

The entry's figure of more than 330,000 evacuated from Dunkirk is not in the saved text, so no figure is given. The article gives the battle as 10 May – 25 June 1940, the armistice on 22 June. | Left out: orders of battle, air forces, the Mechelen incident, Battle of the Alps, the Lancastria sinking, the Franco-British union proposal.
Ancient numbers for Darius's army omitted.
Entry says some 50,000 killed, wounded or missing; article gives 46,000-51,000 total, so only per-army counts are printed.

The article gives two accounts of who killed Jungingen (Dobiesław of Oleśnica per Cronica conflictus; Mszczuj of Skrzynno per Długosz); neither printed. Długosz's account of the Lithuanian retreat as annihilation is contradicted by Cronica conflictus; the text follows the latter. | Left out: the 2014–2017 excavations placing the site south of Grunwald, names of the battle, memorials, sources detail, Nazi propaganda.

The entry says William 'defeated and killed' Harold; the article says the sources contradict each other on how Harold died, so the text hedges the manner of death without denying the entry. | The article gives 'approximately 7 mi northwest' in the lead and '7 mi north' in the body; written 'about 7 miles north'. Left out: armour, the Bayeux Tapestry, orders of battle, Halley's comet, the battle's names.

Article says 'Pope Gregory VIII issued Audita tremendi'; text says 'call a new crusade'. Chronicler Ernoul's claim that Urban III died of shock omitted. 'Saladin said kings do not kill kings' quoted in article.
